verdicts.justification: Reproduced verbatim: hyp.plot(..., font='sans-serif') raises ValueError "sans-serif\n    ^\nParseException: Expected end of text, found '-'  (at char 4)" from FontProperties(family=font) at hypertools/plot/fonts.py:222, BEFORE the guarded findfont try/except, so the docstring-promised helpful ValueError ('is not a recognized installed font family... Tried:') never fires. Independently verified FontProperties(family=['sans-serif']) works ('list form OK: [sans-serif]'), so matplotlib does accept the name in list form -- the crash is hypertools' single-string call path. 'sans-serif' is the most common generic family a user would try; cryptic crash on reasonable use of a documented parameter = major.
commands_run: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; hyp.plot(np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=(10,3)), font='sans-serif', reduce=None, show=False)"

verdicts.justification: Reproduced: 'import hypertools; import hypertools.plot.interactive as i' -> ImportError: cannot import name 'interactive' from 'plot' (unknown location). Also verified type(hypertools.plot) is <class 'function'>; plain 'import hypertools.plot.fonts' succeeds but attribute access raises AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'fonts'; 'from hypertools.plot import fonts' works. Minor: a workaround exists and the shadowing is a common Python-package pattern, but the error is cryptic and undocumented.

Reproduced: font='/Users/jmanning/hypertools/README.md' passes resolve_font silently (os.path.exists branch returns FontProperties(fname=...)) and the failure surfaces only at save time as 'RuntimeError: Can not load face (unknown file format; error code 0x2)' from matplotlib's ft2font, with no mention of the font= argument. Deferred cryptic error on misuse = minor.

Reproduced exactly: mat2colors([0.0, nan, 1.0]) -> [[0.86,0.34,0.34],[0.86,0.3712,0.34],[0.86,0.34,0.34]] -- the finite min (0.0) and max (1.0) get IDENTICAL colors with no warning; mat2colors([[0.5,0.5],[nan,0.5]]) -> [[0.6,0.6,0.6],[0.6,0.6,0.6]] (uniform blend, silent). Evidence w4_nan_hue.png shows an end-to-end hue plot rendered uniformly yellow due to one NaN. Silently wrong colors on reasonable use (hue arrays from real data often contain NaN) = major.

Reproduced exactly: vals2colors(linspace(0,1,5)) -> viridis ranks [0,12,25,37,50]; linspace(0,0.001,5) -> [0,0,0,0,0] (all one color); linspace(0,100,5) -> [0,24,49,74,99]. Color coverage depends on absolute data range. Verified vals2colors/vals2bins are re-exported in hypertools/plot/colors.py line 167 (from .._shared.helpers import vals2colors, vals2bins). Legacy helper, not the main hue path -> minor.

Reproduced exactly: mat2colors(['a','b'], palette=['#ff0000','#0000ff']) -> array(['#ff0000','#0000ff'], dtype='<U7') (strings, not (n,3) floats); RGBA tuple palette -> shape (2,4); 2D input with hex palette -> IndexError: too many indices for array (colors.py:83, base[:, :3] on a 1-D string array). Docstring verified to promise '(n_samples, 3) array of RGB values in [0, 1]'. Contract violation plus crash on a documented palette form, but hex strings still work downstream in matplotlib -> minor.

Reproduced exactly: [[0.25,0.75]] alone -> [0.47,0.7144,0.73] (blend); adding a signed row changes it to [0.34,0.8288,0.86] (pure c1); [[-1,1],[-100,100]] -> two identical rows [0.34,0.8288,0.86]. inspect.getdoc(mat2colors) verified to say only 'Rows are normalized to sum to 1 and each sample's color is the proportion-weighted blend' -- no mention of per-row min-shifting for negatives or its cross-row consequences. Doc gap confirmed.

Reproduced: find_covering_font('日本語のラベル').get_file() -> '/System/Library/Fonts/ヒラギノ角ゴシック W0.ttc' (W0 = thinnest Hiragino weight). Evidence f3_cjk_resolved_vs_default.png visually confirms the resolved CJK text renders hairline-thin and lighter than the regular-weight default-font line below it. Cosmetic weight mismatch, text still legible -> minor.
commands_run: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "from hypertools.plot.fonts import find_covering_font; print(find_covering_font('日本語のラベル').get_file())"

verdicts.justification: Reproduced exactly: hyp.plot(2-level MultiIndex df, linestyles=['-','--'], show=False) emitted 6 warnings, first message 'linestyle is redundantly defined by the 'linestyle' keyword argument and the fmt string "-...'. Documented feature works but is noisy -> minor.

verdicts.justification: Reproduced verbatim, all six probes: mat2colors([]) -> ValueError 'zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity'; mat2colors(5) -> TypeError "'int' object is not iterable"; palette=None -> TypeError "'NoneType' object is not iterable"; n_bins=0 -> IndexError 'list index out of range'; n_bins=-5 -> ValueError 'Number of samples, -4, must be non-negative.'; get_palette_colors('hls', 0) -> IndexError 'too many indices for array'. None name the offending argument. Error-quality rough edge -> minor.

Reproduced (run with -W error::RuntimeWarning to prove silence): colors2groups(np.array([[0.5,0.5,0.5]]), res=1) returned ([(nan, nan, nan)], {(nan, nan, nan): (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)}) with no warning or error. Degenerate parameter, silent NaN -> style.

Reproduced exactly: plotly_draw([(5,4) array], ...) -> '4-col -> 2 scatter3d' (4th column silently dropped, drawn as 3D); plotly_draw([], fmt=[], kwargs_list=[]) -> IndexError: list index out of range at 'ndims = data[0].shape[1]...'. Low-level internal drawing function reachable via the interactive shim; sloppy input contract -> style.
commands_run: .venv/bin/python -c "from hypertools.plot import interactive; plotly_draw 4-col + empty probes"

verdicts.justification: Reproduced: mat2colors(np.linspace(0,10,5)) first=[0.86,0.3712,0.34] last=[0.86,0.34,0.34], max abs diff 0.0312 -- min and max map to near-identical red. Re-rendered the spiral hue plot fresh (hls_wrap.png): spiral start (bottom) and end (top) both render red/salmon and are visually indistinguishable, while intermediate values cycle through the full hue wheel. Circular default for continuous hue is a real perceptual footgun but an explicit palette fixes it -> minor.

Reproduced end-to-end with fresh renders: hue=pd.Series(CJK labels) -> 24 'missing from font(s)' glyph warnings (first: Glyph ... missing from font(s) Arial) and the legend renders empty tofu boxes (series_hue.png); identical labels as a plain list -> 0 warnings and real CJK glyphs (list_hue.png). Direct probe: find_covering_font(pd.Series(['日本語'])) -> None while the same strings as ndarray resolve to Hiragino W0.ttc. Auditor counted 30 warnings, I saw 24 -- count differs, claim holds. Upgraded to major: pd.Series is an utterly ordinary hue input and the output is silently unreadable while the list equivalent works.
commands_run: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "hue=pd.Series CJK vs list, warning counts + savefig both"
Read scratchpad series_hue.png and list_hue.png (fresh renders)

Reproduced exactly: CLAUDE.md line 76 reads '- `interactive.py` - Interactive-mode helpers'; the actual file is a 4-line shim: '# Renamed to hypertools.plot.plotly_backend (HyperTools 1.0). Shim preserves the old path.' followed by re-exports. Doc-accuracy item only.

Reproduced exactly: mat2colors(np.arange(5.), palette=[(1,0,0),(0,0,1)]) -> ValueError: 'palette supplies 2 colors but 100 are required' (colors.py:160 _get_palette). The error at least states the count mismatch; interpolating endpoint colors would be new behavior -> enhancement.
